tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC urban median of (speed − posted limit) over ≥10 s
tolerances.justifiedBy: Speed samples are quantized per 20 Hz frame and the median absorbs free-flow spread; 0.2 m/s covers the posting-limit rounding (0.1 m/s) plus the ±0.04 m/s seeded sample noise, and 5% covers higher urban limits.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC residential median of (speed − posted limit) over ≥10 s
tolerances.justifiedBy: Residential limits are lower, so the same 0.2 m/s posting/quantization floor dominates; the relative part stays at 5% because the estimator uses the same median over a 10 s window.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC curve: intentional 089 lateral demand × class lateral ceiling
tolerances.justifiedBy: The value is reconstructed from p90 class-normalized lateral demand times the 023 sedan ceiling (grip 1.3 × 9.81 m/s²), so the demand percentile and the ceiling rounding dominate; 8% covers demand variation across curve radii.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC explicitly marked approach median speed
tolerances.justifiedBy: An approach window contains deceleration, so the median is a spread statistic rather than a single cruise value; 0.4 m/s covers the approach profile spread and 3% covers faster arterials.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC complete intentional 089 acceleration demand × sedan force/mass
tolerances.justifiedBy: Demand is a dimensionless p90 fraction mapped to the sedan reference ceiling (6500 N / 1400 kg ≈ 4.643 m/s²); 0.15 m/s² covers the trimmed p50 and the class-capability rounding, 5% covers the demand spread.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC complete intentional 089 deceleration demand × sedan brake ceiling
tolerances.justifiedBy: The deceleration ceiling is 8 m/s², so one demand percentage point is 0.08 m/s²; 0.2 m/s² covers the trimmed p50 plus the p90-to-p50 difference and 5% covers stronger braking.

tolerances.context: FREE_TRAFFIC tick-to-tick |SI jerk| samples, trimmed p50
tolerances.justifiedBy: Jerk is differenced at the fixed 60 Hz tick, so a single-frame acceleration change is amplified; 0.3 m/s³ covers the 1/60 s differencing noise and 10% covers the outer-tail trimming of the p50.

tolerances.context: observable stimulus, reactionDurationTicks / 60
tolerances.justifiedBy: The reaction is an integer tick count divided by 60, so one tick is 0.0167 s; the 0.02 s absolute floor is exactly that quantization and 2% keeps the bound proportional for longer reactions.

tolerances.context: LEADER moving episodes fitted as gap = minGap + headway × speed
tolerances.justifiedBy: The OLS slope divides gap quantization (0.01 m seeded noise) by the ego-speed spread (≥15 m/s), giving ~0.001 s; 0.08 s covers gap measurement and lateral offset in the fitted line, 3% covers headway spread.

tolerances.context: LEADER moving episodes, OLS intercept at zero speed
tolerances.justifiedBy: The intercept is the fitted gap at 0 m/s, which extrapolates from the lowest observed speed; 0.15 m covers that extrapolation plus the RMS residual rounding and 3% covers larger gaps.

tolerances.context: LEADER QUEUE_STANDSTILL episodes with both speeds ≤ 0.1 m/s
tolerances.justifiedBy: The queue value is the arithmetic mean of measured standstill gaps, so the 0.01 m seeded measurement noise and the 0.1 m/s stop qualification define a 0.15 m floor; 3% covers longer vehicles.

tolerances.context: LEADER moving episodes with a separately observed speedGain
tolerances.justifiedBy: Speed gain is a mean of observed per-episode ratios in 1/s, not a fit coefficient; 0.05 covers the per-episode observation rounding and 3% covers gains above 1/s.

tolerances.context: certain RED opportunities, compliant HELD / certain denominator
tolerances.justifiedBy: The value is a ratio over a certain opportunity count, so its granularity is 1/N; 0.03 is smaller than one count at the fixture denominators (N ≥ 15) and 2% covers stricter fixtures, not a statistical confidence interval.

tolerances.context: unblocked GREEN departures, (departureTick − onsetTick) / 60
tolerances.justifiedBy: Onset and departure are integer ticks at 60 Hz, so the mean carries a 0.0167 s quantization; 0.02 s is that floor and 3% covers fixtures with few departures.

tolerances.context: certain RED opportunities, mean measured stopLineOffsetM
tolerances.justifiedBy: The stop-line offset is the mean of metre measurements rounded to 0.05 m; 0.1 m is two rounding steps and 3% covers larger offsets.

tolerances.context: certain RED opportunities, mean brakeThresholdMps2
tolerances.justifiedBy: The threshold is a mean of deceleration measurements rounded to 0.05 m/s²; 0.05 is exactly one rounding step and 4% covers thresholds near the 6 m/s² upper bound.

tolerances.context: certain FREE_TRAFFIC STOP_LINE facts, full stops / certain denominator
tolerances.justifiedBy: A full-stop ratio shares the 1/N opportunity granularity; 0.03 is below one count at N ≥ 15 and 2% covers the stricter 1/20 fixtures, without inventing a binomial interval.

tolerances.context: measured dwellTicks of full STOP_LINE stops / 60
tolerances.justifiedBy: Dwell is measured in whole ticks at 60 Hz, so the mean has a 0.0167 s quantization; 0.02 s is that floor and 3% covers dwell times above 1 s.

tolerances.context: certain FREE_TRAFFIC STOP_LINE facts, mean measured offset
tolerances.justifiedBy: Same metre measurement as the RED offset but taken at a STOP line; 0.1 m covers two 0.05 m rounding steps and 3% covers offsets of several metres.

tolerances.context: YIELD interval [max refused, min accepted] of signed 052 separations
tolerances.justifiedBy: Only opposed YIELDED/PROCEEDED facts identify the threshold, and the result is an interval whose endpoints are measured separations; 0.15 s pads the interval-edge rounding and 5% covers wider separations.

tolerances.context: optional LANE_CHANGE interval [max rejected, min completed] front gap
tolerances.justifiedBy: The front gap is measured at the manoeuvre and only an accepted/rejected interval identifies the threshold; 0.3 m covers the gap measurement rounding and 4% covers gaps of tens of metres.

tolerances.context: optional LANE_CHANGE interval [max rejected, min completed] back gap
tolerances.justifiedBy: The back gap uses the same manoeuvre-time measurement as the front gap but a different reference vehicle; 0.3 m covers its own rounding and 4% covers the larger gaps.

tolerances.context: optional LANE_CHANGE interval of observed speedAdvantageMps
tolerances.justifiedBy: The advantage is a speed difference in m/s recorded per optional manoeuvre; 0.15 m/s covers the difference rounding and 5% covers advantages near 10 m/s.

tolerances.context: optional completed manoeuvres, mean cooldownTicks / 60
tolerances.justifiedBy: The cooldown is a measured tick interval divided by 60; 0.05 s allows for manoeuvre-boundary tick assignment and 3% covers long cooldowns up to 30 s.
